article.title: Why Feature Stores Need Point-in-Time Correctness
article.why: 理解 feature store 的歷史取值必須符合 prediction time，避免 time travel 與 leakage。
article.author: OpenAI learning editor

paragraphs.en:
A feature store is meant to make machine-learning features reusable and consistent. Instead of every team rebuilding customer age, thirty-day purchase count, account tenure, or average transaction value from scratch, the organization defines those features once and serves them to both training pipelines and online models. But reuse alone is not enough. The historical value must also be correct for the exact moment when the prediction would have been made. This requirement is called point-in-time correctness.

Consider a churn model trained on customer records from January through June. For each historical prediction date, the model should only see information that was available by that date. If a feature pipeline accidentally uses a customer’s current profile or a later aggregate, the training data contains knowledge from the future. Offline validation may look excellent because the model is receiving information it could never have had in production.

A simple example is a thirty-day spending feature. Suppose the training row represents March 1. The correct feature should use transactions from the thirty days before March 1. If the feature store instead calculates the customer’s latest thirty-day spending when the training dataset is built in July, the March row may contain June or July behavior. The feature name is correct, but its timestamp semantics are wrong.

Slowly changing attributes create another problem. A customer’s membership tier, address, credit limit, or account status can change over time. Training should use the value that existed at the historical prediction timestamp, not the newest value stored today. This often requires effective dates, event histories, or snapshot tables rather than a single mutable record.

Point-in-time joins solve part of the problem. For every training example, the system selects the latest feature value whose timestamp is no later than the prediction timestamp. But engineers must define timestamps carefully. Event time, processing time, and availability time are not always the same. A transaction may occur at noon, arrive in the warehouse at 3 p.m., and become available to the production model at 4 p.m. A truly realistic training set should respect when the feature could actually have been used.

This matters because leakage can hide inside infrastructure that appears standardized. A centrally managed feature store may reduce duplicated code while still generating invalid training data if historical retrieval is not time-aware. Standardization without temporal correctness can make the same mistake more consistent across many models.

Testing should therefore include historical reconstruction. Pick several old prediction timestamps and verify that every feature matches what the production system could have known then. Compare offline feature values with archived online values when possible. Add automated checks for future timestamps, impossible update orders, and aggregates whose windows extend beyond the cutoff.

Good metadata also helps. Feature definitions should document source tables, event time, availability delay, aggregation window, update frequency, and whether historical backfills can revise previous values. These details make review easier and help data scientists understand what “available” really means.

Point-in-time correctness is not only a technical property. It is part of model validity. If the training process sees information from the future, performance estimates are biased no matter how sophisticated the algorithm is. A reliable feature platform therefore needs two promises: the same feature logic can be reused, and historical training data reproduces the information boundary that existed at prediction time.
paragraphs.zh: Feature store 的價值不只是重用特徵邏輯，還要保證歷史訓練資料在每個 prediction timestamp 只使用當時真正可取得的值。event time、processing time 與 availability time 可能不同；如果拿今天的最新屬性或未來窗口回填過去，離線驗證會被 leakage 污染。實務上應使用 point-in-time join、effective date、snapshot／event history，並用歷史重建與 metadata 檢查可用時間邊界。
paragraphs.ja: Feature Storeでは再利用性だけでなく、各予測時点で本当に利用可能だった値を取得できることが重要です。現在の最新属性や将来期間を含む集計値を過去の学習行に入れるとリークになります。event time、processing time、availability timeを区別し、point-in-time joinや履歴テーブル、過去時点の再現テストで情報境界を守る必要があります。

quiz.question: Why can a correct feature name still produce leakage?
quiz.answer: Because the feature may use values from the wrong time period.

quiz.question: What three time concepts may differ?
quiz.answer: Event time, processing time, and availability time.
